title: Periodic graphs and inverse trigonometry
purpose: Read and construct periodic models while keeping angle units, phase, and inverse-function ranges explicit.

lessons.title: Sine and cosine parameters
lessons.objective: Determine amplitude, period, midline, and phase shift and construct a matching sinusoidal function.
lessons.coverage: A*sin(B*(t-h))+D and cosine equivalents, |A|, 2*pi/|B|, reflections, equivalent phase representations, and key points over a full cycle.
lessons.activity: Predict a parameter's effect before changing it; enter numeric parameters, compare a five-point table, and inspect the resulting labeled graph.
families: Extract and interpret parameters from a formula
Construct a sinusoid from a graph description or labeled cycle points
lessons.generatorRules: Require nonzero amplitude and frequency in periodic tasks; use explicit time/angle units. Accept equivalent sine/cosine representations through a reviewed normalization rule.
lessons.commonError: Calling B the period, calling a negative coefficient a negative amplitude, or reading phase from an unfactored argument incorrectly.
lessons.feedback: Factor the argument into B*(t-h), find one full-turn change, and verify the proposed model at two key points.
lessons.checkpoint: Amplitude/midline, period, phase, and model reconstruction.

lessons.title: Tangent and reciprocal graphs
lessons.objective: Predict periods, asymptotes, and domains of transformed tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions.
lessons.coverage: Tangent/cotangent periods, reciprocal relationships to sine/cosine, asymptotes at denominator zeros, and branch behavior between poles.
lessons.activity: Show the underlying sine or cosine values beside a reciprocal table; predict which zero creates a pole before revealing the graph.
families: Find domains and poles on a stated finite interval
Match transformed periodic graphs with their periods and key features
lessons.generatorRules: Derive poles exactly from denominator zeros, split plot segments at poles, and never connect opposite sides of a discontinuity with a line.
lessons.commonError: Assigning the same period to all six functions or drawing continuous segments across poles.
lessons.feedback: Check the denominator and the shortest repeat interval separately.
lessons.checkpoint: A tangent period, reciprocal asymptotes, a domain list, and a graph interpretation.

lessons.title: Inverse trigonometric functions and principal values
lessons.objective: Evaluate arcsine, arccosine, and arctangent within their principal ranges and distinguish them from solving a periodic equation.
lessons.coverage: Arcsine range [-pi/2,pi/2], arccosine range [0,pi], arctangent range (-pi/2,pi/2), domains, and compositions outside the principal interval.
lessons.activity: Compare theta with arcsin(sin(theta)) as theta leaves the principal interval and explain why the returned angle changes.
families: Evaluate exact inverse-trig expressions and compositions
Distinguish one principal value from all solutions on a stated interval
lessons.generatorRules: Use exact special values; enforce input ranges for arcsine and arccosine. General periodic solving is introduced here and completed in m08-l03.
lessons.commonError: Assuming arcsin(sin(theta)) always equals theta or taking an inverse-trig answer as the only periodic solution.
lessons.feedback: Locate the result inside the inverse function's permitted output range before checking its sine or cosine.
lessons.checkpoint: Three principal-value/composition items and one comparison with an equation's solution set.

lessons.title: Signals, frequency, and time shifts
lessons.objective: Fit a simple periodic signal from extrema and timing information and interpret frequency and phase in consistent units.
lessons.coverage: Frequency in cycles/second, angular frequency in radians/second, period, offset, time shift, and choosing a model from idealized measurements.
lessons.activity: Fit a virtual signal with numeric controls, predict its value at a specified time, and compare residuals at provided observations.
families: Recover amplitude, offset, and frequency from extrema and period
Predict a value or time shift and explain equivalent phase descriptions
lessons.generatorRules: Specify enough information for a model up to known periodic equivalence; distinguish ideal exact data from approximate data. Do not introduce sampling theory as a hidden prerequisite.
lessons.commonError: Mixing milliseconds and seconds, mixing frequency and angular frequency, or using an incorrect phase sign.
lessons.feedback: Normalize time units, label the coefficient's units, and evaluate the model at a known peak.
lessons.checkpoint: Parameter recovery, frequency conversion, value prediction, and interpretation of a phase shift.

anchor.prompt: Analyze v(t)=3*sin(4*pi*(t-0.125))+1 with t in seconds.
anchor.answer: Amplitude 3 V, midline 1 V, period 0.5 s, frequency 2 Hz, and shift right by 0.125 s. v(0.125)=1 V and v(0.25)=4 V.

moduleExit: The formula, graph, and table must agree on period, units, and phase; accept mathematically equivalent phase choices.
